note: The ranking fence hits are crates/aft/src/commands/semantic_search/ (request_files.rs new; mod.rs, memo.rs, exact_lane.rs, data_file.rs, nearest_names.rs, rerank/mod.rs, waits.rs), crates/aft/src/search_index.rs and crates/aft/src/parser.rs. One aft_search request now reads each candidate file from disk once: a request-scoped set keeps the bytes the first phase read (pattern verification, the exact pass, lexical exactness) and every later phase (literal presence, matching and declaration lines, the code-reference check through a new FileParser entry that parses the caller's text, snippets, data-file classification, nearest names, exact-memo digest checks, the reranker's candidate text) derives its old answer from those bytes; the ranking and the reranker share one matching-line answer per file and query. No routing, candidate, score, ordering, cap or disclosure changes. The exact lane's prepared-text cache (query-independent preparation keyed by content digest) gains hit/miss counters on the slow-call line and holds 64 MiB instead of 32 MiB; it never changes what a match is. Proof: the search-quality gate passed against the committed reference, and benchmarks/aft-search/compare_builds.py replayed the 6,700 distinct queries of 6,897 recorded aft_search queries on AFT's own checkout against the base build: no result or ranking differed; 4 replies differed only in the base process's watcher_pending gap and its notice, a timing artifact of the response finaliser.
